body:
## Problem

Issue #373: the snap crashes on Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland/X11 hosts:

```
qt.qpa.plugin: Could not load the Qt platform plugin "xcb" in "" even though it was found.
This application failed to start because no Qt platform plugin could be initialized.
```

The snap was built against `core22` (Ubuntu 22.04). The xcb Qt platform plugin links against 22.04 xcb libraries. When the snap runs on a 24.04 host, `dlopen()` fails because the host ABI does not match — producing the misleading "found but could not load" error.

## Solution

Migrate the snap from `core22` + Qt5 to `core24` + Qt6, rebuilding all Qt libraries and platform plugins against the Ubuntu 24.04 ABI.

### snapcraft.yaml changes
- `base: core22` → `base: core24`
- `extensions: [kde-neon]` → `extensions: [kde-neon-6]` (Qt6 + KF6 content snap)
- `architectures:` → `platforms:` (required for core24 in snapcraft 9.x)
- Remove manual `kde-sdk-setup` rsync part — `kde-neon-6` extension provides the SDK automatically
- Build system: `qmake` → `cmake` (qmake is unsupported in KDE Neon 6 extension)
  - `-DBUILD_WITH_KF=ON -DBUILD_KF=OFF`: use system KF6 from SDK content snap
  - `-DPACKAGE_TESTS=OFF`: skip Catch2/GoogleTest FetchContent in snap build
- `kf5-5-110-qt-5-15-11-core22` cleanup snap → `kf6-core24`
- `python3.10` → `python3.12` (core24 default Python)
- Pin `qet-tb-generator` source to `source-tag: v1.31` (issue #202)
- Stage `libxcb-cursor0` — required by Qt's xcb platform plugin since Qt 5.15.x / Qt 6.x; the `kf6-core24` content snap does not bundle it

### cmake changes (from this PR)
- `cmake/build: make Qt::GuiPrivate (PDF hyperlinks) optional` — the `kde-qt6-core24-sdk` snap does not ship Qt6 private headers; guarded behind a `QET_PDF_PRIVATE_HEADERS` compile flag so builds without private headers skip link-injection silently

## Commit structure

This PR sits on top of **PR #505** (cmake Qt6/KF6 support + C++ compatibility fixes) and adds only three commits of its own:

| Commit | Scope |
|--------|-------|
| `cmake/build: make Qt::GuiPrivate optional` | cmake + source — guards private-header usage absent from the snap SDK |
| `snap: migrate to core24, kde-neon-6, cmake build` | snapcraft.yaml only |
| `snap: stage libxcb-cursor0` | snapcraft.yaml only — independently cherry-pickable |

No cmake or C++ source changes are duplicated from PR #505.

## Build proof

Ran the cmake `override-build` step against the Qt6/KF6 source tree (PR #505 applied) inside an isolated Docker container (Ubuntu 25.04, Qt6 + KF6 from apt — equivalent to what the `kde-neon-6` extension provides):

```
cmake -B build -S . -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
      -DBUILD_WITH_KF=ON -DBUILD_KF=OFF -DPACKAGE_TESTS=OFF
cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
DESTDIR=/tmp/install cmake --install build
```

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| cmake configure (Qt6 detected) | ✅ `QT_VERSION_MAJOR: 6` |
| Compile 395/395 targets | ✅ zero errors |
| Link `qelectrotech` | ✅ |
| Install binary + elements + translations | ✅ |

## Sequencing note

Per discussion with @scorpio810 this PR is **parked until after the Qt5 stable release**. It is kept open and rebased so it merges cleanly immediately after PR #505 when the project is ready to move to Qt6.

The near-term fix for #373 on the current Qt5/core22 snap is **PR #517** (one-line: stage `libxcb-cursor0`).

Closes #373 (Qt6 path). Depends on #505.

commits.messageBody:
- find_package(QT NAMES Qt6 Qt5): try Qt6 before falling back to Qt5
- Replace qt5_create_translation/qt5_add_translation with the
  version-agnostic qt_create_translation/qt_add_translation aliases
- Scope lupdate source scan to sources/ to avoid Qt6 lupdate choking
  on modern JS syntax in the doxygen-awesome-css submodule
- Rewrite cmake/fetch_kdeaddons.cmake to auto-detect Qt major version
  and select KF5 (Qt5) or KF6 (Qt6) accordingly; the new file accepts
  both BUILD_WITH_KF5 (legacy name) and BUILD_WITH_KF; when BUILD_KF=OFF
  it uses system-installed KF6 packages, BUILD_KF=ON fetches from git
- Update target_link_libraries to use KF_PRIVATE_LIBRARIES (works for
  both KF5 and KF6) instead of the KF5-only KF5_PRIVATE_LIBRARIES

Tested: cmake + ninja build to completion with Qt 6.8.3 + KF6 on
Ubuntu 25.04 inside Docker. Binary links against libQt6*.so.6 with no
missing dependencies. Closes the CMake half of issue #402.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: cmake: add Qt6 and KDE Frameworks 6 support

commits.messageBody:
Qt6 removes implicit conversions and merges previously distinct types;
all changes below are guarded with #if QT_VERSION where needed so the
Qt5 build path is unchanged.

qgimanager.h / qgimanager.cpp
  Qt6 makes QVector<T> an alias for QList<T>, so the pre-existing
  QList<> overloads of manage() and release() become duplicate
  signatures. Guard the deprecated QList overloads under Qt5 only.

sources/diagramview.cpp
  QTextStream::setCodec() was removed in Qt6. Qt6 defaults to UTF-8,
  so the call is guarded out under Qt6 with no behaviour change.

sources/machine_info.cpp
  QDirIterator::next() returns QString; comparing it to integer 0 with
  operator> is ambiguous in Qt6. The intent was simply to count files
  while iterating; rewrote the three loops to call next() and increment
  unconditionally (hasNext() already guarantees a valid entry).

sources/qetxml.h
  QUuid is no longer transitively included in Qt6. Added explicit
  #include <QUuid>.

sources/titleblocktemplate.cpp / titleblock/templatescollection.cpp
  QDomDocument::setContent() returns QDomDocument::ParseResult in Qt6
  (not bool). ParseResult has an explicit operator bool, so it cannot
  be assigned to a bool variable. Moved the call directly into the if
  condition where the explicit conversion is allowed.

sources/titleblock/templateview.h
  QGraphicsGridLayout and QGraphicsLayoutItem are no longer
  transitively included in Qt6. Added explicit includes.

sources/TerminalStrip/physicalterminal.cpp
  std::min(int, qsizetype) is ambiguous in Qt6 because QList::size()
  returns qsizetype (64-bit) not int. Added static_cast<int>.

sources/TerminalStrip/GraphicsItem/terminalstripdrawer.h / .cpp
  QUuid and QHash not transitively included in Qt6; added explicit
  includes. QPolygonF{v} brace-initialisation fails when the
  QPolygonF(QList<QPointF>) constructor is explicit; changed to
  QPolygonF(v).

sources/ElementsCollection/elementslocation.cpp
  The Qt6 branch already used QRegularExpression but still called
  QRegExp methods (.exactMatch(), .cap()). Fixed to use
  QRegularExpressionMatch (.match(), .hasMatch(), .captured()).

sources/pdf_links.cpp / print/projectprintwindow.cpp
  Added a #warning on Qt6 builds flagging <private/qpdf_p.h> for
  manual verification. The header compiled and linked successfully
  under Qt 6.8.3; QPdfEngine::drawHyperlink() remains available.

sources/qetgraphicsitem/ViewItem/projectdbmodel.cpp
  QVector<int>(Qt::DisplayRole) creates a vector of size 0 (since
  Qt::DisplayRole == 0), not a vector containing DisplayRole. Fixed
  to {Qt::DisplayRole}.

Build verified: cmake + ninja on Ubuntu 25.04 / Qt 6.8.3 / KF6.
Binary confirmed Qt6-linked via ldd. Startup confirmed via
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen --version and --help.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: fix(qt6): fix C++ source incompatibilities for Qt6

commits.messageBody:
The kde-qt6-core24-sdk snap does not ship Qt6 private headers, so
Qt::GuiPrivate is unavailable in the snap build environment.  Guard
all three QPdfEngine / drawHyperlink call sites behind a cmake-driven
QET_PDF_PRIVATE_HEADERS define that is set only when Qt::GuiPrivate
actually exists.  Builds without private headers silently skip the
link-injection step; builds with full Qt6-dev headers are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The snap was built on core22 with the Qt5 KDE content snap
(kf5-5-110-qt-5-15-11-core22) and qmake.  This broke on Ubuntu 24.04
because the xcb Qt platform plugin compiled against core22 libraries
fails to load on a 24.04 host — SIGABRT with "Could not load Qt platform
plugin 'xcb' even though it was found" (issue #373).

Changes:
- base: core22 → core24 (matches Ubuntu 24.04 host ABI)
- extensions: kde-neon → kde-neon-6 (Qt6/KF6 content snap)
- platforms: amd64/arm64 (replaces deprecated 'architectures' for core24)
- Remove kde-sdk-setup part — kde-neon-6 extension provides the SDK
  automatically via kde-qt6-core24-sdk + kf6-core24-sdk build snaps
- Build system: qmake → cmake (qmake is not supported by KF6);
  uses cmake Qt6/KF6 fixes from PR #505
  - -DBUILD_WITH_KF=ON -DBUILD_KF=OFF: use system KF6 from SDK snap
  - -DPACKAGE_TESTS=OFF: skip Catch2/GoogleTest FetchContent in snap build
- PYTHONPATH: python3.10 → python3.12 (core24 default Python)
- cleanup part: kf5-5-110-qt-5-15-11-core22 → kf6-core24
- qet-tb-generator: add source-tag: v1.31 (reproducible builds, #202)

Depends on PR #505 for cmake Qt6/KF6 support and C++ compatibility fixes.
Closes #373.

commits.messageBody:
Qt's xcb platform plugin (libqxcb.so) requires libxcb-cursor.so.0 at
runtime since Qt 5.15.x / Qt 6.x.  The kf6-core24 content snap does not
bundle this library.  Without it dlopen() of the plugin aborts at startup.
